assumptions: the prediction is a fixed permutation of all agents
Algorithm 2 changes only its unlearned-agent scan order to that permutation
R(sigma) is the number of agents on which LearnHyperplane is actually invoked
the stated multiplicative bound assumes R(sigma) >= 1; R=0 uses the paper's n-query footnote
claim: Algorithm 2[sigma] is correct and uses O((n + m log(1/epsilon)) R(sigma)) queries for R(sigma)>=1, with smooth linear degradation in operational record quality.
failure_conditions: the measured LearnHyperplane count differs from R
a returned lottery is not unanimously acceptable
an exact count exceeds the R-dependent finite envelope
the R=0 exception or a negative control is missed
paper_anchors: Permutation Predictions definition of H(sigma) and R(sigma)
